Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with its normed additive commutative group structure and a measurable structure satisfying BorelSpace. Let V:E→ℝ be twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. Let α,β be nonnegative real numbers and η a real number. The input assumptions are α>0, α≤β, η>0, βη≤1, and, for every x,v∈E, α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖². There is no positive-dimension assumption, no strict exclusion of the endpoint βη=1, and no additional caller assumptions about measures, kernels, spectral gaps, subspaces, inverses, or operators.

Define μ to be the normalized exponential tilt of Lebesgue measure on E by −V. Define J as the pushforward of μ⊗stdGaussian(E) under (x,g)↦(x,x+√η g), and let ν be the second marginal of J. If (X,Y) has joint law J, define Λ to be the law of (Y,2X−Y). Separately, define F:E×E→E×E by F(x,y)=(x,2x−y). Thus Λ uses (y,2x−y), whereas F retains x as its first coordinate.

Let H=L²(J;ℝ). Let mY be the sigma algebra pulled back from E by the second-coordinate projection, and let HP be the closed subspace lpMeas(ℝ,ℝ,mY,2,J) of H. Let P:H→H be conditional expectation onto this sigma algebra, followed by the inclusion HP↪H. The required measurability/comap relation and inherited Hilbert-space structures are internally supplied. The second-coordinate projection is measure preserving from J to ν; let M:L²(ν;ℝ)→H be its linear isometric pullback, so M sends u to the class of (x,y)↦u(y).

The conclusion first asserts that μ,J,ν are probability measures, that HP equals the linear range of P, and that P f=f for every f∈HP (with the natural inclusion in H). It then produces one joint collection of the following witnesses. Each later witness and identity refers to the same earlier witnesses throughout.

There is a Markov kernel S:E→Measure(E) such that, for every state y∈E, S(y) is exactly the normalized exponential tilt of Lebesgue measure by x↦−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η). This equality is every-state, not merely ν-almost everywhere. S is a conditional kernel for the actual law Λ, and both the first and second marginals of Λ equal ν. In particular the claimed kernel belongs to that reflected joint law, rather than being only an abstract operator representation.

There is a real linear isometric equivalence e:L²(ν;ℝ)≃HP whose inclusion into H equals M on every u∈L²(ν;ℝ). There is a real linear isometry U:H→H with (Ug)(z)=g(F(z)) for J-almost every z, for each g∈H; U is involutive and its associated bounded operator is selfadjoint. There is a bounded real linear operator T:L²(ν;ℝ)→L²(ν;ℝ) which is selfadjoint and, for each u∈L²(ν;ℝ), satisfies ‖Tu‖≤‖u‖, (Tu)(y)=∫u(x) S(y)(dx) for ν-almost every y, and ∫Tu dν=∫u dν. The almost-everywhere assertions are per observable; no one exceptional set working for all observables at once is asserted.

Using this same U and the previously defined P, define A:HP→HP by orthogonally projecting U applied to the inclusion of HP back onto HP. Define B:HP→H by B=(I_H−P)UP composed with the inclusion HP↪H. Then A=eTe⁻¹, A is selfadjoint, ‖Af‖≤‖f‖ for every f∈HP, and P(Bf)=0 for every f∈HP. All products of bounded endomorphisms here and below mean composition.

There is a positive bounded operator Γ on L²(ν;ℝ) with Γ²=I−T² and ΓT=TΓ. Positivity includes selfadjointness and a nonnegative quadratic form. Define ΓP=eΓe⁻¹ on HP. Then ΓP is positive, ΓP²=I_HP−A², ΓP A=AΓP, and B*B=ΓP², where B*:H→HP is the Hilbert adjoint of the displayed B.

There is q∈L²(ν;ℝ) represented by the constant function 1 ν-almost everywhere, with Tq=q and ⟨q,u⟩=∫u dν for every u∈L²(ν;ℝ). Put qP=e q and HP0=ker(f↦⟨qP,f⟩) inside HP. Give HP0 its inherited complete real Hilbert-space structure. Define γ=2√(αη)/(1+αη). For every f∈HP, membership f∈HP0 is equivalent to ∫e⁻¹f dν=0. Also ΓP qP=0 and γ>0. These are conclusions, and HP0 is the exact centered subspace defined using this same qP and e.

There is a bounded operator ΓP0:HP0→HP0 whose inclusion into HP agrees with ΓP on every element of HP0. It is positive, ΓP0−γ I_HP0 is positive, and ΓP0 is a unit in the bounded-operator algebra. There is a bounded operator Inv:HP0→HP0 with Inv ΓP0=I_HP0 and ΓP0 Inv=I_HP0, with ‖Inv‖≤1/γ, and with Inv selfadjoint. Both inverse identities concern the same Inv and the same ΓP0. There is a bounded operator A0:HP0→HP0 whose inclusion into HP agrees with A on every element of HP0; A0 is selfadjoint, commutes with ΓP0, satisfies A0²+ΓP0²=I_HP0, and commutes with that same Inv. None of these restriction, coercivity, invertibility, or commutation properties is an input hypothesis.

Put Hperp=ker P inside the whole joint Hilbert space H, with its inherited complete real Hilbert-space structure. This is the conditional-mean-zero subspace, not the entire globally zero-integral subspace of H. There is a bounded B0:HP0→Hperp such that its inclusion in H equals B applied to the inclusion HP0↪HP. There is a bounded V0:HP0→Hperp with V0=B0∘Inv and B0=V0∘ΓP0, with V0*V0=I_HP0, and with ‖V0 f‖=‖f‖ for every f∈HP0. This is an isometry into Hperp. The statement supplies neither surjectivity onto Hperp nor the reverse identity V0V0*=I_Hperp.

There is a bounded R:H→Hperp whose inclusion in H is Rg=g−Pg for every g∈H. For every g in the full ambient space H, the same ambient adjoint B*:H→HP satisfies B*g=i0(B0*(Rg)), where i0:HP0↪HP is the inclusion and B0*:Hperp→HP0 is the Hilbert adjoint of B0. This is an all-g identity; the domain of B* is not restricted to Hperp or to the range of V0. Define D:Hperp→Hperp by D=R∘U∘i_perp, where i_perp:Hperp↪H is inclusion. For every h∈Hperp its ambient value is i_perp(Dh)=U(i_perp h)−P(U(i_perp h)). The operator equality V0*∘D=−(A0∘V0*) holds on the whole Hperp. It is not limited to h in the range of V0.

Finally, for every f∈H whose real Bochner integral ∫f dJ is zero, there is fP∈HP0 such that i0(fP) is exactly condExpL2(f) as an element of HP. Thus its ambient inclusion also equals Pf. For this f, put fperp=Rf∈Hperp and fV=V0* fperp∈HP0, using the same globally chosen R and V0. Then B*(i_perp fperp)=i0(ΓP0 fV), i0(ΓP0 fV)=ΓP(i0 fV), ‖f‖²=‖fP‖²+‖fperp‖², and ‖fV‖≤‖fperp‖. Only fP is newly existentially chosen after the universal quantifier over centered f; all kernel, pullback, involution, Markov-operator, root, inverse, restriction, factorization, and compression witnesses precede this quantifier and must work together.

All spaces and operators are real. All L² elements are almost-everywhere equivalence classes, and the displayed representative equalities use the stated measures J or ν. The theorem permits zero-dimensional E and trivial centered subspaces, and its identities use the identity operator on the exact space indicated. Its only explicitly displayed lower-bound/inverse constant is γ=2√(αη)/(1+αη), with inverse norm bound 1/γ; β enters the Hessian upper bound and the allowed step-size condition. No additional rate, full-complement invertibility, onto factorization, pointwise observable equality, or source-specific interpretation is part of this reconstruction.
objects: The input data are E, its real normed inner-product and Borel measurable structures, the potential V, nonnegative α and β, and real η. The defined measures are the normalized tilt μ, Gaussian joint pushforward J, second marginal ν, and reflected law Λ. F fixes the first coordinate and reflects the second. H=L²(J;ℝ); mY is the second-coordinate comap sigma algebra; HP is its closed measurable subspace; P is conditional expectation included in H; M is the second-coordinate pullback. Produced witnesses, in their dependency order, are S, e, U, T, Γ, q, ΓP0, Inv, A0, B0, V0, and R. Defined objects depending on them are A, B, ΓP, qP, HP0, γ, Hperp, D, and, for each centered joint observable f, fperp=Rf and fV=V0* fperp. The final fP is produced separately for each centered f. The inclusions HP↪H, i0:HP0↪HP, and i_perp:Hperp↪H must remain distinct.
domains: E is an arbitrary finite-dimensional real inner-product space, including dimension zero. Both joint laws live on E×E. μ,ν and the statewise kernel values S(y) live on E. V:E→ℝ and the Hessian test variables x,v range over all E. H=L²(J;ℝ), L²(ν;ℝ), HP⊆H, HP0⊆HP, and Hperp=ker(P)⊆H are the exact Hilbert spaces. e:L²(ν)≃HP, M:L²(ν)→H, U:H→H, T and Γ:L²(ν)→L²(ν), A and ΓP:HP→HP, B:HP→H, ΓP0,Inv,A0:HP0→HP0, B0,V0:HP0→Hperp, R:H→Hperp, and D:Hperp→Hperp. B*:H→HP, B0* and V0*:Hperp→HP0. The adjoint identities quantify the full H or Hperp shown, not a range-only subdomain. The final f ranges over all H subject only to ∫f dJ=0.
quantifiers: For every admissible E,V,α,β,η satisfying precisely the initial hypotheses, define the displayed measures/spaces/maps. Probability, range, and fixed-point assertions hold; then there exists one S satisfying its Markov, every-y explicit value, conditional-law, and marginal conditions; there exists one e compatible with M; there exists one U satisfying its per-g AE action, involution, and selfadjointness; there exists one T satisfying all per-u actions, contractions, and integral identities; there exists one Γ satisfying the global root/commutation conditions and all ΓP identities; there exists one q satisfying the AE constant, fixed-point, and all-u pairing conditions; there exists ΓP0, then one Inv, then one A0, then one B0, then one V0, then one R, satisfying all dependent identities. With those same witnesses fixed, D is defined and its all-h/domain-wide identities hold. For every globally centered f∈H there exists fP∈HP0 with the stated conditional-expectation equality and, using defined fperp and fV, all final identities/inequality. Initial universal x,v; every-state y kernel equality; per-observable g and u AE statements; all f∈HP, all f∈HP0, all ambient g∈H, and all h∈Hperp retain their distinct scopes. No existential witness in this chain is a caller premise.
assumptions: Caller assumptions only: E carries NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace ℝ, FiniteDimensional ℝ, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures; V is ContDiff ℝ 2; α,β∈ℝ≥0; α>0 after coercion to ℝ; α≤β; for every x,v∈E the second Fréchet derivative satisfies α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖²; η∈ℝ with η>0 and βη≤1. No probability normalization assumption, conditional-kernel assumption, isometric equivalence assumption, involution assumption, operator/root/inverse/existence assumption, positive-dimensional assumption, or nontrivial-subspace assumption is supplied. The comap-order Fact and inherited complete Hilbert structures are internal constructions.
conclusion: μ,J,ν are probabilities; HP=range P and P fixes HP. The same produced Markov S has the exact every-state normalized density exp(−V((y+x)/2)−‖y−x‖²/(8η)), is a conditional kernel of Λ, and Λ has both marginals ν. Produced e equals the actual pullback M after inclusion. Produced U is the AE composition with F, involutive and selfadjoint. Produced T is selfadjoint, contractive for every input, agrees AE with integration against S for every input, and preserves each integral. A=eTe⁻¹ is the displayed selfadjoint contractive compression; B=(I−P)UP|HP lands in ker P. Γ≥0, Γ²=I−T², ΓT=TΓ; ΓP=eΓe⁻¹≥0, ΓP²=I−A², ΓP A=AΓP, B*B=ΓP². q=1 AE, Tq=q, ⟨q,u⟩=∫u dν; qP=e q defines exact HP0, whose centering equivalence holds; ΓP qP=0 and γ>0. ΓP0 is the positive restriction, ΓP0≥γI, is a unit, and has the same selfadjoint two-sided inverse Inv with norm ≤1/γ. A0 is the selfadjoint restriction of A, commutes with ΓP0 and Inv, and A0²+ΓP0²=I. B0 restricts B into Hperp, V0=B0 Inv, B0=V0 ΓP0, V0*V0=I and V0 preserves every norm. R is the full residual projection g↦g−Pg with codomain Hperp. B*g=i0 B0* Rg for every ambient g. D=R U i_perp has the stated residual ambient action and V0*D=−A0V0* on all Hperp. For every globally centered f there is centered fP giving its conditional mean, while fperp=Rf and fV=V0*fperp satisfy B*i_perp fperp=i0ΓP0 fV=ΓP i0 fV, exact squared-norm decomposition, and ‖fV‖≤‖fperp‖.
scopes: Every-state kernel formula is stronger in scope than the per-u ν-AE operator formula, and the per-g U formula is J-AE. Each AE assertion is for the specific observable being quantified. Λ is the reflected law (Y,2X−Y), while F(x,y)=(x,2x−y); these maps are not interchangeable. HP is the conditional measurable macroscopic subspace. HP0 is its centered kernel defined with qP; Hperp is ker P, the conditional complement. A0,ΓP0,Inv act only on HP0. B* acts on the whole joint H, and its identity uses R to recover the intrinsic complement input. D and the V0*D identity act on the whole Hperp, including inputs outside range V0. V0 is only an isometry into Hperp; no onto/reverse-product claim. Global mean zero in the final implication is an additional condition on each f, not a redefinition of Hperp. All witnesses are simultaneous nested output data, with the same Inv used in both inverse identities, A0 commutation, and V0=B0 Inv; final fP may depend on f. Boundary values βη=1 and αη=1 are not excluded; neither dimension zero nor trivial HP0 is excluded. No source identity or fidelity verdict is reconstructed.
constant_dependencies: The Hessian constants α,β are nonnegative, with α strictly positive and α≤β. The step-size η is strictly positive and obeys βη≤1. The normalized joint construction uses √η. The reflection coefficient is exactly 2. The kernel uses midpoint factor 1/2 and quadratic denominator exactly 8η. The positive coercivity constant is γ=2√(αη)/(1+αη)>0 and the inverse norm bound is exactly 1/γ. There is no dimension-dependent constant in the displayed conclusion. β affects the admissible data and step size but does not appear in the displayed γ. No larger parameter regime, added higher-derivative constants, alternative normalizations, or additional convergence-rate constant is asserted.
